card.intuition: A subagent is an agent spawned by another agent via a tool call that runs in its own session with its own context window and reports a single tool result back. Subagents exist to isolate context, not to compose hierarchies — they cannot spawn further subagents.
card.analogy: A specialist you dispatch on a scouting trip: they burn their own fuel exploring, then come back with a two-line summary, leaving your own fuel tanks untouched.
card.time_complexity: O(noise in a disposable window): noisy work like a broad search or long file-reading runs in the subagent's window, so only the final report lands in the parent, reducing per-turn parent cost.
card.space_complexity: O(disposable window + compact report): the finite parent context holds just the summarized result instead of pages of raw tool output.
when_to_use: When grep results are blowing out the parent context
When a broad search or long file-reading expedition produces pages of tool results that matter only long enough to find the answer
When several independent pieces of work can fanned out concurrently across subagents
gotchas: The report is a secondary source — the parent gets the subagent's account, so anything the report leaves out is invisible to the parent
A subagent cannot spawn further subagents; the tree is one level deep
Distinct from a handoff — the parent expects a return, while a handoff has no return path

steps.label: Spawn
steps.annotation: The parent agent spawns a subagent via a tool call to run work in its own context window.

steps.label: Run
steps.annotation: The subagent burns its own context window on noisy search and file-reading output.

steps.label: Report
steps.annotation: The subagent reports a single compact tool result back to the parent.

steps.label: Return
steps.annotation: Only the final report stays in the parent's context while the noise remains in the disposable window.

exercise.prompt: Write a function that compresses a noisy result into a compact report for the parent agent, keeping only the matching lines.
hints: Return the filtered list that holds the lines the parent actually needs
The report should be small, since it will land in the parent's ready-only context
exercise.test_code:
lines = ['src/app.py matches', 'node_modules log', 'src/main.py matches']
assert summarize(lines, 'matches') == ['src/app.py matches', 'src/main.py matches']
assert len(summarize(lines, 'zzz')) == 0
